● Files now go into Lanes, and the lane comes first. You make a lane, then drop
  files into it, and each product only reads the lanes linked to it. The UI, the
  backend, the migration and the tests are all done. Nothing is committed.

  What you'll see in the Studio
  - Lanes window. It's first in the menu bar and in the dock ("+ Lane"). It also
    opens on its own in a project with nothing connected yet.
  - Make a lane. Describe the files in your own words, e.g. "front pics of me
    every morning". The model suggests a name, a short note, the analyzer and
    the products the lane feeds. Code then checks it: feeds that can't read that
    kind of file are dropped, and duplicate names or unknown analyzers are
    blocked. You review and edit the suggestion before anything is saved. The
    "set it up yourself" link skips the model.
    - Both steps show in the Observatory as lanes.suggest_one (model) and
      lanes.check_one (code).
  - Lane cards show the name, note, analyzer, thumbnails, files, how many are
    read, how many are being read, and the products the lane feeds. A lane that
    feeds nothing is shown in red.
  - Click a lane to open it. You can drop files in, see every file with its read
    status and row count, change what it feeds, delete files, or remove the
    lane. While files are being read, the window refreshes every 3 seconds.
  - The Sources window now only covers live inputs: screen, weather, sensors and
    webhooks. Choosing "Files" in Add source sends you to Lanes.

  How links drive products
  - A product linked to lanes reads only its own lanes' files. It also still
    reads anything that isn't a file (screen, sensors) and files uploaded before
    lanes existed. A product with no links reads the whole project, as before.
  - Links stay in sync on their own:
    - Turning a product on links every lane that can feed it, and turning it off
      unlinks them.
    - A new lane feeds every product that's on and can read it, unless you
      choose its feeds yourself.
  - Migration 0020 linked your existing lanes and is applied to the real
    database. "Pedestrian area clip" now feeds the object detection dataset, the
    density heatmap and the people count.

  Checks
  - The typecheck and lint are clean.
  - All 181 tests pass, including 7 new ones for lanes.
  - I clicked through the real app in a browser with no console errors:
    - Pedestrian area: the lane, its file (read, 56 rows) and its 3 feeds show
      correctly.
    - My body log: I typed "front pics of me every morning" and the real model
      suggested "Morning front photo". It picked the body analyzer and the right
      body products (Body progress, Day 1 vs today, Check-in streak). I didn't
      create it, so that's yours to try. The call left two real traces in that
      project's Observatory.
  - /design STU-06 shows all 8 states. I just fixed thumbnails spilling out of
    narrow cards: C:\Users\OS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--argus\08984255-411c-4
    0f5-ae48-ee40403decd2\scratchpad\lanes-design2.png

  Known limits
  - If you remove every link from a product, it goes back to reading the whole
    project.
  - Video files show an icon, not a thumbnail.
  - Public replays on /explore don't filter by lane yet.

  To try it: open My body log in the Studio, click New lane, and describe your
  photos. What's the next step in the redesign?

● Sensors, feeds and screens now come in through a lane like files do, and the
  "+ Source" button is gone. A new project starts with "Make a lane first". All
  185 tests pass, the type check and lint are clean, and migration 0021 is
  applied.

  What changed for the user
  - A lane is the first thing you make. Each lane has a "Comes from" input:
    files, screen share, weather feed, sensor or webhook. Making a weather,
    sensor, screen or webhook lane sets up its live input behind it. Removing
    the lane stops that input.
  - The old Sources window is deleted. A live lane's setup now opens inside the
    Lanes window. It shows when data last came in, a Run now button, the
    latitude/longitude or asset form, screen capture, and the webhook command.
    The latitude and longitude boxes now have visible labels.

● Yes. The timeline becomes the main way to read the whole project. Every lane,
  every AI step and every product update gets its own row, and you can click any
  mark and play the whole thing back.

  line, dots where it changed)    │

                                │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┸────────────────
  ───────────────────────────────┘

  Rows

  - Lanes: one row per lane.
    - Files lanes: a dot for each file added (●).
    - Screen lanes: a bar while capture is running, with a tick for each frame
      taken.
    - Weather, sensor and webhook lanes: a small mark for each reading.
    - Dot states: hollow while waiting, spinning while being read, filled when
      done, red when it failed.
  - Observatory: one row for each kind of step. ◆ is a model call, ■ is code, ▲
    is a tool. A failed step shows ✕ in the same row, so failures are easy to
    spot.
  - Data products: one row per product, drawn as a mini sparkline of its value
    over time, with a dot wherever it changed. Products that are missing a lane
    show why, right in the row.

  Click anything and the whole Studio follows

   click ● (a file in Front cam)
     ├─► SCENE      shows that image, with the model's boxes on it
     ├─► OBSERVATORY scrolls to the ◆ that read it: model, input size, output, 
  tokens
     ├─► PRODUCTS   the right-hand cards show their values at that moment
     └─► TIMELINE   draws the chain:  ● file ──► ◆ AI read ──► ■ fusion ──► ◉ 
  People count +1
  Clicking a ◆ or a product dot works the same way and traces the chain back to
  the file it came from. This is the "how did this number happen?" story in one
  click.

  Playback

  - Play moves the playhead along. The scene shows each file as its dot passes,
    the Observatory lines appear as they happened, and the product cards tick up
    live.
  - Skip quiet jumps over gaps, so a week of daily photos plays in about 20
    seconds.
  - Speed can be 1×, 4× or 16×, or step: ◀◀ and ▶▶ move from one event to the
    next.
  - Follow live: while a lane is capturing or reading, the playhead stays at
    "now" and new dots appear as they come in.

  Hover and zoom

  - Hover a dot to see a tooltip with a thumbnail, the filename (owner only),
    the time, and "read by muse-spark · 3 detections".
  - Zoom with the mouse wheel or the day / hour / minute buttons. When zoomed
    out, dense marks merge into one numbered bubble ("●12"). Click it to zoom
    in.
  - Expand (⤢) makes the timeline taller so it takes over half the screen.
    That's useful for reviewing the whole project.
  - Drag a range to select it. The scene then shows that range as a filmstrip,
    and the products show totals for just that window.

  How it sits in the Studio

  ┌ LANES ────────────┬ SCENE (preview) ─────────────────┬ DATA PRODUCTS ─────┐
  │ cards + setup     │ image/frame + selected product    │ small live cards   │
  │ thumbs, drop here │ overlay                           │ value at playhead  │
  │                   ├ OBSERVATORY (detail) ─────────────┤                    │
  │                   │ the selected step, full detail     │                    
  │
  ├───────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────┤
  │ TIMELINE: lanes ● · observatory ◆■▲ · products ▁▃▅  · playhead ┃ · chain   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ┘

  Because every step now shows on the timeline, the middle Observatory pane
  becomes the detail view for the selected step: what went in, what came out,
  tokens, and the Observations it wrote. The timeline is where you browse, and
  the Observatory pane is where you read one step in full.

  On Explore the timeline is the same but starts playing automatically.
  Filenames are hidden, and private media shows a 🔒 thumbnail in the tooltip
  and the scene.

  Is this buildable with the data we already have?

  Mark: ● file dots
  Comes from: uploads.createdAt, laneId, status
  Already stored?: yes
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Mark: screen bars / readings
  Comes from: Observations with a sourceId or no upload
  Already stored?: yes
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Mark: ◆ ■ ▲ ✕
  Comes from: traces (kind, name, time, error)
  Already stored?: yes
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Mark: chain file → AI → product
  Comes from: traces → Observation ids it wrote → upload
  Already stored?: mostly. Traces record the Observation ids they wrote. The
  link
  from a product dot back to its trace is computed from those ids.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Mark: product sparkline
  Comes from: the product's manifest over time
  Already stored?: yes (the replay already does this)

  It needs no new data, only joins in the replay loader.

  If you're happy with this, I'll build it component-first: a STU-05 v2 Timeline
  surface in /design showing these states (empty project, files only, live
  capture, a failed step, zoomed out with merged marks, a selected chain,
  playing). Then the three-pane STU-01 around it, and only after that wire it
  into /studio and /explore.

  data product comes out. To keep it from overwhelming people, it opens simple
  and you open more only when you want it.

  The simple timeline has one row per lane, plus one Products row. A dot is a
  file or a reading. It stays hollow until the AI has read it, then fills in. ▲
  marks the moments a product changed. That's all a new user sees.

  Click a dot and the middle pane tells that file's story in four lines: the
  file went in, the AI looked at it, code checked the result, and these products
  changed. The right-hand cards highlight what that file added. The full trace
  is one click away, under "open in Observatory".

  Three levels, so nobody is overwhelmed

  SIMPLE (default)            LANE STEPS (click a lane name)          EVERYTHING
  (Observatory mode)
  ─────────────────           ──────────────────────────────          
  ─────────────────────────────
  ▣ Front cam  ● ● ●● ●       ▾ Front cam                             ▣ Front 
  cam   ● ● ●● ●
  ▭ Front desk ═══════          in        ●    ●  ●●   ●              ▭ Front 
  desk  ═══════
  ☁ Weather    ·   ·            AI read   ◆    ◆  ◆◆   ◆              ☁ Weather 
     ·   ·
  ▤ Products   ▲  ▲ ▲           checked   ■    ■  ■■   ■              AI   model
     ◆ ◆ ◆◆◆ ◆ ◆
                                out  ▲ People count  ▲ Objects         CODE 
  fusion    ■   ■   ■

  ask/mcp      ▲
                              ☁ Weather    ·   ·                      ✕    
  failed         ✕
                              ▤ Products   ▲  ▲ ▲                     ▤ People 
  count ▁▂▃▅▅▃▂
                                                                      ▤ Objects 
      ▪ ▪▪ ▪
    "what came in, what       "how did the AI handle                 "every 
  step, every model
     came out"                 THIS lane?"                            call", for
  power users / demo

  - Simple: about 4 rows for most projects. It answers "is my data being read,
    and is anything coming out?"
  - Lane steps: opens one lane, or several, into in → AI read → checked → out.
    This is the "how does the AI analyze this lane" view: you can follow a
    column straight down from one file to the product it fed.
  - Everything: today's full Observatory: all traces, failures and tools, plus
    one sparkline per product.

  The setting is remembered for each person. On Explore the default is Lane 
  steps for the main lane, so visitors see the AI working right away.

  Playback in simple mode

   ▶ play:  playhead moves → dots fill in as the AI reads them → ▲ appears → 
  right-hand card ticks up
            the preview flips through each photo as its dot passes, the model's 
  boxes fade in
   skip quiet: a week of daily photos plays in ~20 s

  Small screens / first visit

  - If the project has no lanes yet, the timeline is one line: "Your lanes show
    here as soon as data comes in". The rest of the screen guides you to "+
    Lane".
  - The timeline can collapse to one strip: playhead, scrubber and ▲ marks,
    about 28px tall.

  When this looks right, I'll build it component-first in /design:
  1. STU-05 v2, the timeline: simple, lane steps, everything, empty, collapsed,
     a selected file, playing.
  2. STU-01 v2, the three-pane Studio around it.
  3. Then wire it into /studio/[id] and /explore.

  Built:
  - Studio layout: lanes on the left, preview with "How the AI read it" in the
    middle, data products on the right, and the timeline across the bottom.
  - Timeline: three levels: Simple, Lane steps and Everything. Clicking a dot
    shows that file in the preview, tells its step-by-step story, and highlights
    the products it added to.
  - Public shares: the same layout, read-only. File names are hidden, body lanes
    are locked, and media shows only if the owner shares it.
  - /design: STU-05 now shows each timeline state side by side, and STU-01 and
    EXP-02 use the new layout.

  Fixed during the browser check:
  - Squeezed timeline: the timeline ran until "now", so the Pedestrian share's
    3-minute clip was crammed into the left edge of a 22-hour axis. It now ends
    at the project's last activity, or at now while work is still running.
  - Wrong "after the playhead": a clicked item could still show "This is after
    the playhead". The playhead now lands just past it.
  - Chart overflow: the open product card's chart spilled over the cards below
    it.
  - Crowded "Lane steps": it opened sub-rows for live lanes that have no AI
    steps. Now only lanes the AI worked on open, and any lane can still be
    toggled.
  - Readings count: live lane cards said "1 readings". They now count the actual
    rows, for example "36 readings".
  - /design image errors: the sample widgets requested images that don't exist,
    which caused the 404s. They no longer do.

  Tests: bun test --coverage was failing before this work. Bun applies the 95%
  threshold to each file, and several earlier files were under it. I added four
  test files and one test each to two existing files:
  - tests/lib/studio-timeline.test.ts covers the new timeline loader.
  - tests/lib/share.test.ts covers what a public share may show, including body
    photos staying private.
  - tests/lib/kits.test.ts covers the body and persona widget helpers.
  - One test in video.test.ts checks that cleanup still finishes when a storage
    delete fails. One in body.test.ts covers the body check-in job.

  Still open:
  - On Maya's Harbor project, weather and sensor readings go into the lane but
    feed no product, so the story says "not in a product yet".
  - Screen-capture frame jobs still write no traces.
  - Videos show a camera icon in the preview, not a playable clip.
  - The loading skeleton still shows the old layout, not the three-pane one.

  in London, 2–3 April 2025. A mobile crane lifts the jib while riggers in
  orange work on it, and an excavator digs below. The photos and video are by
  Acabashi on Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), and the project description
  credits them.

  How it was made: I logged into Studio as Lena in a test browser. The 12 photos
  went onto the photo lane's card in four batches, as if added through the day,
  and the clip went onto the video lane's card. Every step went through the
  normal pipeline with real muse-spark model calls, and every step is in the
  Observatory.

  What the AI found:
  - Objects: 99 found: 55 people, 25 excavators, and 16 cranes it split into
    tower, mobile and plain crane.
  - People count: 1 to 4 people in each of the 16 video frames.
  - Rust: the surprise. Without being asked, the model flagged rust on the
    crane's white equipment housing in two photos, which set off two
    investigations. That's the model's claim and I haven't checked it against
    the photos.

  - − shrinks a panel to its header bar and gives the other panel the room. ⤢
    makes a panel fill the middle.
  - To get both panels back, press the lit button again or double-click a header
    bar.
  - A minimized steps panel still shows its step count in the bar, and "Open in
    Observatory" stays there for the owner.
  - Each viewer's choice is remembered in their browser, like the timeline mode,
    and survives a reload. It works in both /studio/[id] and /explore/[slug].
  - /design EXP-02 has a new variant that opens with the preview maximized.

  Timeline audit: what caused the double line and flicker
  1. Two lines. The grey shade that covers the future moved a few times a
     second, while the white playhead moved every frame. Its edge showed as a
     second line that jumped along behind the playhead. Both now move every
     frame together.
  2. Lines out of step. The tracks keep room for a scrollbar but the scrub strip
     above them didn't, so the playhead in the strip and the one in the tracks
     drifted apart toward the right. Both rows now have the same width.
  3. Jank. Every lane row redrew every frame because its click handlers were
     remade each time. Those handlers are now stable and the rows are cached, so
     only the playhead moves while it plays. The playhead and shade now slide
     instead of forcing the whole timeline to re-lay out each frame.
  4. Playhead lost on scroll. When the timeline was tall enough to scroll, the
     playhead stopped partway down. It now runs the full height.

● I made all four fixes and checked them in a real browser at 1920×1080 on the
  Moira Close replay. There were no console errors.

  Rendering (the root cause)
  - What was wrong: the replay's exact time was stored in React state, so the
    whole studio re-rendered about 60 times a second.
  - The fix: the exact time now lives outside React. Only the playhead line, the
    shading, the scrub fill, the clock text and the seek slider follow it, and
    they update themselves directly. React only re-renders when the playhead
    moves one step (480 steps per replay).
  - Preview: a new picture only appears once it has fully loaded, together with
    its own label and findings. Over 14 seconds of playback it never showed a
    half-loaded picture and never fell back to "Nothing has come in". The next 4
    pictures load ahead of time.
  - Timeline: while it played, the playhead line, the shading and the scrub line
    stayed within 0.4px of each other.

  Lanes and products now add to the list instead of rebuilding it
  - Widget lists: the event feed, rows table and friction log identified rows by
    their position, so each new row rebuilt every row and replayed the entrance
    animation. They now use a row key that stays the same as new rows arrive
    (rowKeys in src/widgets/kit.ts, which has a test). Over 12 seconds, 16 rows
    were added to the products panel and 27 dropped off the end, because each
    list only shows a limited number of rows.
  - Lane panel: it no longer rebuilds while the replay plays. 5 new thumbnails
    appeared and only one old one was removed, and thumbnails no longer
    lazy-load, so they don't flash blank.

  Several products open at once
  - Each card's chart opens and closes on its own click, and the rail header has
    an "open all / close all" button.
  - The preview's findings order follows the product you clicked last.
  - Picking a product's mark on the timeline also opens its card.

  The "Named" strip is now one line
  - It reads like NAMED  person ×3 96%  crane 98%: repeated names become one
    chip with a count and the best confidence.
  - The "no boxes" note moved into the hover tooltip.

  Type-check, lint and all 206 tests pass. Nothing is committed.

  Your idea: nicer product widgets plus a resize handle. I'd do both:

   PREVIEW                       ┃ DATA PRODUCTS        close all
                                 ┃ ● Object detection  ▾  ⤢
                                 ┃   15 records  ▁▃▅▇
          (picture)              ┃ ┌ chart, drag ═ to resize ┐
                               ◀━╋━▶                         │
                                 ┃ └══════════════════════════┘
   NAMED person×3 96% crane 98%  ┃ ● People count      ▸  0

  - Drag handle between preview and products: it's remembered per viewer, and
    double-click resets it. A wider rail gives the charts room.
  - Each open card can be resized by dragging its bottom edge. The fixed card
    height cuts widgets off today: in the screenshot, the detection board's
    "SEEN OVER TIME" chart is cut off.
  - Card polish:
    - a coloured header strip in the product's colour
    - the number ticks up as rows arrive
    - a short "+3" flash when the playhead adds records
    - a proper empty state instead of "Nothing yet at this point"
    - charts set to fill their card rather than a fixed size

  Want me to go ahead with all of it? I'll build it in /design first, as the
  component-first rule requires.

● The resize handles and the nicer product cards are built and working.

  Why the line lands away from the photo you clicked
  - The dot is when the photo came in. The white playhead jumps to when the AI
    finished reading it, the right edge of the dashed band.
  - It goes there on purpose: that's the moment the preview, the findings and
    the step list have something to show. At the dot itself, the AI hadn't read
    the photo yet.
  - Nothing said that before, so both ends of the band are now labelled:

            came in 13:34:21 [●]─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─│ read 13:34:3x ▸
                              ┆      AI reading        ┆█ playhead

  If you'd rather the line stay on the dot, I can do that and show a "not read
  yet, jump to result ▸" link in the preview instead.

  Resizing
  - Preview ↔ products: drag the thin line on the rail's left edge to make the
    products rail wider. It can grow to half the studio, and double-click resets
    it. In my test I dragged it from 336px to 590px and it stayed 590px after a
    reload.
  - Each open chart: drag the grip under it to make it taller (120–720px,
    default 220px). Each product keeps its own height, and double-click resets
    it. The cut-off detection board now scrolls inside its card or can be
    dragged taller.
  - Both sizes are saved per viewer in the browser.

  The cards
  - There's a colour strip in the product's colour along the top, and the card
    you clicked last gets a light tint of its colour.
  - The count runs up to each new value instead of jumping, and a "+n" floats up
    once when the playhead adds records. Both are switched off for viewers who
    turn off motion.
  - A chevron shows whether a card is open, and the header shows "· n kinds"
    when a product has more than one kind of record.
  - The sparkline now spans the whole card, as steps with a soft fill.
  - The empty state is a dashed box saying "No records yet at this point. Press
    play to watch it fill."

● I made the studio and explore load faster. Explore now loads in about 0.4s,
  the studio in about 0.9s. These were measured on a production build of the
  current code (bun --bun next build + start). The studio isn't committed.

  Why it was slow
  - The loading screen was from the old dashboard. While a project loaded, you
    saw a layout that didn't match the studio. Then everything jumped into
    place.
  - The whole studio waited for its slowest window. Lanes, Products, Observatory
    and Agents were all loaded before anything showed, even though they're
    closed popups.
  - The studio read the project's data one wave at a time. It checked who you
    are, then read the products, then their data.
  - Explore did every database read again on every visit, even though a shared
    replay only changes when the owner changes it.
  - Server code was shipped to the browser. The database library (drizzle) and
    the form-checking library (zod) were sent to every page because a few
    browser files imported them by accident.

  What I changed
  - New loading screen (studio-skeleton.tsx, in /design STU-02) with the same
    frame as the studio: lanes, preview and story, products, timeline. Nothing
    jumps when the data arrives. I screenshotted it at 1920×1080; it has no
    console errors.
  - Each window loads on its own. The studio shows as soon as its own data is
    in, and a closed window can't hold it up. A window that isn't ready yet
    shows a small placeholder.
  - The studio reads everything at once. Its database reads start at the same
    time as the sign-in check, so there's one wait instead of several. Nothing
    is shown unless the project belongs to the person signed in.
  - Explore replays are cached for about a minute. Turning sharing off, changing
    media sharing or deleting the project clears that link's cache straight
    away, so a private replay never lingers.
  - Server code is out of the browser. I moved the shared lists into small files
    the browser can use. I also replaced the browser-side zod checks with plain
    functions, and new tests check they give the same result as zod. That's
    about 37KB less JavaScript per page (studio 428→391KB, explore 405→368KB).
  - The database pool now allows 20 connections instead of 10, since a studio
    opens with a few dozen reads at once. In dev the pool is also reused across
    reloads instead of opening a new one each time.

  Numbers

  ┌────────────────┬────────┬────────────────────────────┐
  │                │ Before │           After            │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ Explore (dev)  │ ~4.2s  │ ~0.8s                      │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ Explore (prod) │ n/a    │ ~0.4s, page itself 30–50ms │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ Studio (prod)  │ n/a    │ ~0.9s                      │
  └────────────────┴────────┴────────────────────────────┘

  I didn't measure a production build before the changes, so prod has only
  after-numbers.

  The studio in dev (next dev) still takes about 4s, because the dev server
  compiles its JavaScript while you wait. That doesn't happen in a real build.

  Type checks, lint and all 210 tests pass. I stopped the production server I'd
  started on port 3100.

        1 +# Meta models: research and ARGUS integration plan            
        2 +                                                              
        3 +Research date: 2026-10-28. Status: proposal; no runtime integr
          +ation implemented by this document.                           
        4 +                                                              
        5 +## Capability and project fit                                 
        6 +                                                              
        7 +**An author describes the data product they want, adds source 
          +data, and ARGUS selects compatible Meta capabilities, runs a v
          +alidated analysis, and records an evidence-backed replay.**   
        8 +                                                              
        9 +This fits ARGUS: sources become Observations, fusion relates t
          +hem, manifests define products, and widgets display the result
          +s. For the hackathon, authors run the analyses in Studio; visi
          +tors watch stored results on `/explore` without sign-up or new
          + model calls. See [HACKATHON.md](HACKATHON.md) and [ROADMAP.md
          +](ROADMAP.md).                                                
       10 +                                                              
       11 +Recommendation: first integrate the hosted Meta Model API fami
          +lies through separate adapters. Start with Spark + SAM + trans
          +cription in one recorded story. Add image generation only to a
          + product where an explicitly generated illustration helps expl
          +ain the data. Keep a place for research models without making 
          +GPU hosting a prerequisite.                                   
       12 +                                                              
       13 +## Research scope and evidence                                
       14 +                                                              
       15 +The requested starting point was the [Meta developer overview 
          +with the supplied team/project context](https://dev.meta.ai/do
          +cs/overview?team_id=1312144450995364&project_id=84025514238949
          +8). That exact URL could not be fetched by the research reader
          +. The public [overview](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/overview) and
          + its model-specific developer guides were readable and form th
          +e primary basis of this plan.                                 
       16 +                                                              
       17 +Documentation availability is not proof that our project's API
          + key can call every model. No authenticated inference, billing
          + check, package installation, or GPU deployment was performed.
          + Account access and actual response shapes remain implementati
          +on spikes.                                                    
       18 +                                                              
       19 +Sections below separate documented Meta behavior from proposed
          + ARGUS design. Proposed capability IDs, files, Observation typ
          +es, and database additions do not exist merely because they ap
          +pear here.                                                    
       20 +                                                              
       21 +## 1. What Meta offers                                        
       22 +                                                              
       23 +### Hosted models relevant to ARGUS                           
       24 +                                                              
       25 +| Model ID | Documented role | Proposed ARGUS use |           
       26 +| --- | --- | --- |                                           
       27 +| `muse-spark-1.3` | Multimodal understanding, reasoning, stru
          +ctured output, tool calling | Default planner, source interpre
          +tation, image review, evidence-based explanations |           
       28 +| `muse-wonder-1.0` | More complex, longer agentic work | Opti
          +onal difficult planning/reasoning step after evaluation |     
       29 +| `sam-3.1` | Image/video segmentation and tracking | Object m

       31 +| `muse-image-1.0` | Image generation and editing | Clearly la

  - Before (dev server, so only a rough comparison): the landing page took ~1.6s
    to show its largest content and ~6.4s to settle. It downloaded every replay
    picture at full size, about 630 KB each and up to 4 per card, including
    ones you never saw.
  - Smaller pictures: replay cards now get a 480 or 960px WebP copy (~38 KB
    instead of ~630 KB). Only the first picture loads; the rest load when you
    hover the card.
  - Cached Explore list: the shared-project list is cached. It refreshes when
    you share, unshare, rename, change media or delete a project.
  - Carousel: the examples carousel no longer re-measures the page every frame,
    and it stops when it's off-screen. The scroll runs at 61 fps with no long
    tasks.
  - Fixed image sizes: the landing images ask for the right size for the screen.

  Docs:
  - New /docs page with 12 guides, each as numbered steps with a real
    screenshot:
    - watch a replay
    - create a project
    - pick data products from the catalog
    - add a lane
    - drop files on a lane
    - read the studio
    - use the timeline
    - see every step in the Observatory
    - manage data products
    - Ask ARGUS
    - present your projects
    - share a replay
  - FAQ in three groups: basics, how the AI works, and your data and privacy. It
    covers that models propose and code computes, that counts are estimates,
    why there are no boxes, that replays make 0 model calls, that body lanes are
    never public, what a step records, CSV download, and file types up to 500
    MB.
  - Landing page: the old "About ARGUS" section (it still said "choose Sources")
    is replaced by six guide cards with screenshots, the first two FAQ groups,
    and links to /docs. I deleted src/components/landing/use-cases.tsx; it
    wasn't tracked by git, so it can't be restored from history.
  - Links: Docs is now in the nav and both footers.
  - Previews: you can check all of it in /design under DOC-01 (guide), DOC-02
    (FAQ) and DOC-03 (docs page), with LND-06 for the landing section.

● I built a new demo project, shared it publicly, and checked it end to end on
  :3000 only.

  What to show the judge: "Roundabout at US-14 / US-61", now Omar Haddad's
  project. A real drone video of a busy roundabout goes in, and two Meta models
  work together on it.

  Public replay: http://localhost:3000/explore/M9GqA5HrZU10. It autoplays, uses
  no model calls ($0.00), and shows the video with SAM's outlines.

  What the AI did:
  - Muse Spark suggested the lane, "Roundabout drone view", from one plain
    sentence.
  - The browser sampled 19 frames, and Spark named what was in each one: 133
    cars, 10 trucks, 1 person.
  - SAM 3.1 then outlined every vehicle with 28 calls, for 228 outlines. SAM
    found 225 cars where Spark had counted 133. That's a good line for judges:
    one model names things, the other finds every one of them.
  - All of it shows step by step in the Observatory and in the "How the AI read
    it" panel, with no errors.
  - The products are Object footprint, Density heatmap and Object detection
    dataset. Each can be downloaded as CSV.

  Pitch for the judge: "Drop in any traffic video. Spark says what's there, SAM
  outlines every vehicle, and code turns that into counts and maps. You can
  replay every step and see what each model returned."

  The clip is CC0 from Wikimedia Commons ("Roundabout 14 61"), so turning on
  media in the replay is fine. The video is 27 MB and the model calls cost about
  $0.10–0.15.

  Bugs I found and fixed along the way:
  - Phantom "Screen share" lane: my SAM step recorded the picture size under the
    name frame, and the timeline treated that as a screen capture. I renamed
    the field to size, and the timeline now only accepts text keys, so the older
    steps already saved are handled too.
  - Outline labels covered the cars: I made them smaller.
  - Demo login cards: they now show the current names, "Roundabout at US-14 /
    US-61" and Lena's "Moira Close crane build".

  All 235 tests pass, and typecheck and lint are clean. Nothing is committed.

  Gap you should know about: Vehicle traffic dashboard and Road safety event
  feed are labelled "supported" but nothing computes them, so they show 0
  records in every project. They need vehicle tracking and a count line, which
  ARGUS doesn't have yet. I took them out of this project so judges don't see
  empty cards.

  Next, if you want:
  1. Build a real "vehicles in view per frame" count from SAM's outlines, and
     mark the two empty products as planned until then.
  2. Make the density heatmap grid finer. It's 14×8 now, which is too coarse to
     show the roundabout's shape; a finer grid would draw the ring from where
     the cars actually were.

● The timeline now ends where the project's data ends, so there's no more empty
  stretch running up to today.

  Why it happened: the end of the timeline was set by the latest event of any
  kind, and that included setup changes. Choosing a data product again or
  renaming a lane after the work was done counted as activity. On the roundabout
  project, a product change made about 12 minutes after the last frame
  stretched the timeline from 17:23 to 17:38. Only 17:23 to 17:25 had anything
  on it.

  What changed (in src/components/explore/public-studio.tsx):
  - The timeline now runs from the first activity to the last file read or job
    finished, plus 2% padding so the last dot isn't cut off at the edge.
  - Setup changes no longer move the end.
  - While work is still running, the end still follows the current time, so live
    work stays in view.
  - Your Studio and the Explore replays use the same component, so both are
    fixed.

  Checked on :3000:
  - Roundabout, in your Studio and on Explore: the timeline now shows 17:23 →
    17:25. The dots and product markers fill the strip right up to the end, and
    there are no console errors.
  - Lena's crane build: most of her timeline is still blank. Most of the work
    sits at the start, and a few steps sit right at the end. Those late steps
    are real: SAM located objects in old pictures after a product was turned on
    later. They aren't setup changes, so the timeline still has to reach them,
    and the space in between is genuinely empty.
  - Type checks, lint and tests pass (235 tests).

  If you want Lena's kind of gap closed up too, I can collapse long empty

✻ Worked for 4s · done 1:05 AM

> can u suggest what should we add mroe ??                                      

● Here's what I'd add, ranked by how much it would impress judges. ARGUS is
  meant to show Meta's models working together, visible in a replay, so the top
  three lean that way.

  Best for the demo

  1. A narrated replay. While we analyse, Llama writes a short caption for each
     step, like "Spark saw 7 cars, SAM found 11; code kept SAM's outlines". The
     captions are saved, so on /explore they play as subtitles under the
     timeline with no model calls. Judges would understand what the AI is doing
     without reading the Observatory.
  2. A "models disagree" product. On the roundabout, Spark counted 133 cars and
     SAM found 225. We can turn that gap into a data product: count per frame
     from each model, where they disagree, and which one code trusted. Few demos
     show two models checking each other, so this one would stand out.
  3. Tracking vehicles across frames. Code matches SAM's outlines from one frame
     to the next, so the same car keeps its ID. That unlocks the Vehicle
     traffic dashboard (cars per minute, which exit they take) and the Road
     safety feed (near misses). Both are dead on video right now.

  Breadth (more kinds of sources)

  4. An audio lane. Meta's speech model turns a voice memo or a video's audio
     track into timestamped transcript Observations. That proves ARGUS handles
     more than vision. A spoken site report next to Lena's crane photos would
     fuse nicely.
  5. A live camera lane. A webcam or phone stream, with dots appearing on the
     timeline as it runs. That's a strong live moment if you demo in person.

  The product getting smarter

  6. Describe a product in words. For example: "how long trucks stay on site". A
     model proposes a manifest, code validates it against the real
     Observations, and you get a new widget. This is phase 2 from the roadmap.
  7. Alerts. You set a rule like "more than 5 people near the crane", code
     checks it, and the AI explains why it fired. Alerts would appear as markers
     on the timeline.

  My pick is 1 + 2: they're about a day of work together, and they make the
  replay tell the story without anyone explaining it. Tracking (3) is next,
  because it brings two existing products to life.

  Which ones should I build?
